a4530.speech: Believes that if Ilaje farmers pivot to salt-tolerant crops, they might reclaim productivity: “The salt can be a blessing, if channelled right. Certain rice species, for example, thrive in salty environments. With proper research and education, we can help women farmers understand what will grow and how.” ; also advocated for the use of genetically modified cash crops and more climate-resilient agriculture to boost local economies and food security.

a4530.speaker: Stella Ojulowo, 48, farmer in Oroto
a4530.speech: “As saltwater dey kill ham, we still dey plant. The small wey survive, we go chop.”

a4539.speaker: South Sudan National Bureau of Standards (SSNBS)
a4539.speech: Has ordered the return of six trucks carrying 3,840 bags of white sorghum back to Tanzania after the consignment was deemed unfit for human consumption upon arrival at the Nimule entry point; the agency said it acted swiftly to prevent the substandard grains from entering the local market.

a4539.speaker: SSNBS laboratory analysis
a4539.speech: Revealed that the sorghum failed to meet national safety and quality standards due to physical damage, contamination with foreign matter, and poor overall condition.

a4539.speaker: Ashgan Paulina Edward, Acting Director General for Technical Operations at SSNBS
a4539.speech: “The Nimule station detected trucks coming from Tanzania, holding 3,840 packs of white sorghum, which discovered it’s not fit for human consumption.” ; “The truck is coming for humanitarian aid, and the inspection revealed that the consignment has impurity, and then have like foreign matter plus insects, like the consignment is totally damaged.” ; narrated that the consignment entered Nimule on March 21 when they discovered that it was of poor quality, and that SSNBS attempted to resort it but found the consignment was totally damaged ; “Therefore, we told them that there is no way either to export it to the country of origin or to dump it in Nimule. And they went with the first option, whereby we supposed to export it to the country of origin.” ; “So, we sent the trucks back. And this is one of our efforts to make sure that which is coming to South Sudan is meeting the standard specification and the quality requirement. So, this act based on the EAC standard.”

a4668.speaker: Mary Olive Smith '88, documentary filmmaker and owner of Flying Pup Productions
a4668.speech: Says the path to her art was both obscured and illuminated by her varied passions: “I was given the advice that sometimes the policy line wouldn't align with my heart. I had always been involved with film and music, and I knew that was truly what filled my heart, so I kept following my passions, and everything fell into place. It turned out I had knack for the technical and logistical side of filmmaking—the grind of it all. I was never doing it for the glamour; I love the day to day.”

a4668.speaker: USAID study
a4668.speech: Documented an estimated 36,000 to 39,000 women in Ethiopia live with obstetric fistula, with more than 3,000 additional new cases occurring each year.

a4668.speaker: Mary Olive Smith '88, documentary filmmaker
a4668.speech: On A Walk to Beautiful: says it is both a story of healing and hope; “By far, it was the best experience of my life. There's something about childbirth that is universal—you can go to the most remote part of the world and connect with another mother.”

a4668.speaker: Mary Olive Smith '88, documentary filmmaker
a4668.speech: On short-form work: “I've always tried to tell the in-depth story no matter how long the end result is. The challenge of adapting my storytelling technique into very short pieces was fascinating. I still prefer long form, but I learned you actually can tell a lot in a short time.”

a4668.speaker: Mary Olive Smith '88, documentary filmmaker
a4668.speech: On the NOVA project in Baltimore: “Culturally, it was the most difficult thing I've ever done. I had to gain trust from people who have lived very different lives from my own.”

a4668.speaker: Mary Olive Smith '88, documentary filmmaker
a4668.speech: On her future work: “I can't work for free, but I wish I could. I feel lucky to get to work on these issues and tell important stories. Whether I'm in Baltimore or Ethiopia, I listen with sincerity to what people have to say. I'm 53 now, and I hope I'll keep making films for another 30 years. People in my field tend to never quit.”

a4733.speaker: Gambians Against Looted Assets (GALA) (statement by its Communications Unit)
a4733.speech: Issued a scathing statement, accusing PURA of shielding telecom companies while undermining the public: "PURA's decision is destructive, unacceptable, and a direct attack on consumer welfare" ; argue that the price floor will disproportionately harm students, business owners, and content creators who depend on affordable internet for their livelihoods ; emphasized that PURA's role as a regulator is to ensure fairness and sustainability, not to enable exploitation by mobile operators ; dismiss PURA's defence as a pretext to favor corporate profits, arguing that the price hike will make internet access unaffordable for many, and accuse PURA of failing to uphold its mandate to prioritize consumer interests ; has called for an immediate reversal of the policy, pledging support for the journalists' demands and urging PURA to protect Gambian consumers.

a4733.speaker: Journalists from multiple Gambian media outlets
a4733.speech: Have joined the outcry, demanding justice and fairness for internet users ; highlight the internet's critical role in education, entrepreneurship, and digital content creation, particularly for low-income communities ; warn that the new tariff risks exacerbating economic inequality and stifling opportunities in a country where digital access is increasingly vital.

a4733.speaker: Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) of The Gambia
a4733.speech: Defends the regulation, claiming it reinforces quality-of-service standards and protects consumers from the adverse effects of unsustainable pricing.

a5116.speaker: Jang Sungamin, South Korean senior secretary for future strategy
a5116.speech: Using the "teach a man to fish you will feed him for a lifetime" analogy, stated that South Korea has mastered the technique and wants to share it with Africa.

a5401.speaker: Chris Brown, American musician
a5401.speech: Made clear that the life of fame has had a major impact on his mental health, explaining that he likes to sneak out at night so that he can feel like an ordinary human being; explained that despite his great success there are times when he feels he has lost his freedom to live an ordinary life, and that to feel happy he changes his appearance with a big hat, sunglasses or by covering his face so he can walk down the street unrecognised ; explained that doing so gives him time to change his surroundings, to think, or to eat in an ordinary restaurant like an ordinary person, without pressure and without paparazzi cameras ; explained that this is not about hiding who he really is but about returning himself to a human state, because fame can make an artist feel like a product and forget that he is a human being who needs freedom, calm and an ordinary life; added that sneaking out at night reminds him that he still has a life outside the stage, the cameras and social media.

a5401.speaker: Chris Brown, American musician
a5401.speech: Called on other artists to do justice to the other side of their lives outside of stardom, because he believes there is still much that is good and valuable in being "Chris" and not "Chris Brown" who is known worldwide.

a5401.speaker: Billnass, Tanzanian hip hop musician
a5401.speech: Gave advice to upcoming artists, urging them to be patient because the industry is full of many bad things beyond the fame: "To all Young People, my little ones and my friends who have been blessed with various talents, before entering any industry connected with fame in Tanzania!! Pray hard to God to give you the strength of patience and a spirit of endurance!! Here there is every kind of war, betrayal, devilishness, oppression, starting from stakeholders, managers, distribution companies, labels, etc." ; "The matter of getting rich or getting money through this work is not as easy as you hear, but getting stress, losing your life, getting diseases, becoming confused or falling into various addictions is easier than making money; it is good to be very careful and to enter the industry while ready, but do not stop putting God first." ; "Because you may be struggling in order to help your family, when in fact you are going to bring a disaster in which your family will be the ones with the burden of suffering to help you," he wrote.

a5859.speaker: Sarah Houssein Ahmed, Chair of the Board of Directors of the DERE Institute
a5859.speech: Opened the proceedings by declaring: "It is always a pleasure for me to welcome you on behalf of the whole DERE team; your presence among us delights us and comforts us in the continuation of our actions. We are gathered today to take stock of DERE's prospects, launched in April 2023 as a 'think tank' type institute to contribute to the development of public policies and to the country's economic growth. The DERE institute aims to be a societal project, promoting culture, dialogue, and the sharing of experience and expertise. Our policy is to become a privileged partner both for political decision-makers and for private operators and development partners. To do this, however, the Institute needs your support to realise its ambitions: moral support such as your presence and participation, technical support such as expertise, and above all financial support, since without financial resources an organisation cannot develop and professionalise. We thank all the sponsors and the governmental, private and international cooperation partners who have accompanied us since the beginning. Thank you."

a5859.speaker: Mahamoud Ahmed Sougueh, Director General of the DERE Institute
a5859.speech: Declared: "It is a real pleasure for me and my team to welcome you, a moment of particular importance for our Institute. Before presenting our 2024-2025 outlook to you, allow me to tell you that these four small letters DERE have a deep meaning for us. We went through several stages before being able and daring to appear before actors such as yourselves to discuss programmes and projects. Since 2019, DERE has organised debates of ideas involving political, economic, social, cultural and academic decision-makers, in interaction with citizens. We are aware of the scale of the task. We positively aim to influence public policies, to establish spaces for reflection, sharing and influence between citizens and the government. Our objective is to promote the active participation of young people and women through the PJAA (Programme for Young Actors) and PLF (Female Leadership Programme) programmes, programmes that aim to empower young people as actors of their economic, social and cultural integration, and to strengthen, in line with the national Gender policy, the institutionalisation of the female voice through the development of female leadership."

a5862.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (post on X)
a5862.speech: Announced that the US Department of State, along with Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), made this decision after a six-week review of the agency's activities ; "The 5,200 contracts that are now cancelled spent tens of billions of dollars in ways that did not serve, (and in some cases even harmed), the core national interests of the United States" ; "In consultation with Congress, we intend for the remaining 18% of programmes we are keeping (approximately 1,000) to be administered more effectively under the State Department."

a5862.speaker: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA), Nigeria
a5862.speech: Earlier announced its plan to strengthen its domestic HIV response and produce HIV-related medical tools, including test kits and antiretroviral drugs.

a5862.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (earlier reports)
a5862.speech: Reported that intervention programmes were abruptly suspended, community health workers lost their jobs, and USAID health workers deployed to hard-to-reach areas were recalled.

a5862.speaker: Wale Edun, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy of Nigeria
a5862.speech: Disclosed that FEC also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment.

a5984.speaker: Organisers of the Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Fair
a5984.speech: After two editions, an evaluation was carried out by the organisers, who concluded that the results were mixed.

a5984.speaker: Nadine Dako Tamadaho, Minister of Youth Employment and the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises
a5984.speech: Indicated that the meeting with journalists aims to set the tone for the event that will take place next November; insisted that the contribution of institutions is important for the survival of businesses ; “Today, more than 8,800 businesses have been created, but unfortunately many of them do not survive.” ; Said the theme “Financing SMEs: Challenges and Prospects” is very important and requires that institutions, SME support organisations and promoters join hands for the success of the sector’s activities.

a6089.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghanaian Minister of Finance
a6089.speech: has reiterated the government's focus on food security and economic stability ; described food security as a national priority, emphasizing the need for collaborative efforts to address rising food prices and their impact on vulnerable populations. "More than one million Ghanaians are at risk of food insecurity due to skyrocketing prices."

a6089.speaker: World Food Programme (statistics cited)
a6089.speech: referenced alarming statistics from the World Food Programme that more than one million Ghanaians are at risk of food insecurity due to skyrocketing prices.

a6089.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghanaian Minister of Finance
a6089.speech: highlighted the Goldbod initiative, describing it as a transformative project aimed at improving gold export tracking, stabilizing the cedi, increasing foreign exchange inflows, and creating jobs. Acknowledging past challenges within Cocobod, he stated, "We cannot let isolated setbacks overshadow the invaluable contributions Cocobod has made to Ghana's development or derail promising initiatives like Goldbod." ; expressed confidence that Goldbod would soon be fully operational, delivering long-term stability and inclusive growth.

a6089.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghanaian Minister of Finance
a6089.speech: reaffirmed Ghana's commitment to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program, noting that corrective actions had been taken to address structural slippages inherited from the previous administration. "We are committed to ensuring fiscal discipline and achieving key economic targets under the IMF program."

a6089.speaker: Cassiel Ato Forson, Ghanaian Minister of Finance
a6089.speech: emphasizing the importance of international cooperation in achieving sustainable development. "Canada's support in agricultural modernization and resource management will complement our domestic efforts to stabilize the economy and achieve food security."

a6265.speaker: Zambia Air Force (ZAF)
a6265.speech: Says outdoor operations are key to fueling economic activities through enhanced security.

a6265.speaker: Lt Gen Colin Barry, ZAF Commander
a6265.speech: Said outdoor operations are critical in enhancing the Air Force’s strategic capabilities and operational readiness ; hailed the Air Force’s commitment to conducting exercises in diverse and realistic environments such the Northern Province ; said he was honoured to witness the incredible dedication and professionalism demonstrated by the Air Force personnel during outdoor operation in Kasama ; said outdoor operations were not only about defense but also played a crucial role to training, readiness, and strategic capabilities, enabling the force to effectively respond to a wide range of challenges ; said outdoor operations also contribute to national security objectives including humanitarian assistance and disaster relief by responding swiftly in times of crisis ; “Outdoor operations are the cornerstone of our preparedness. It is here, in the field, that we validate our training, test our equipment, and hone the skills necessary to face the diverse challenges that may arise.”

a6265.speaker: Maj Misheck Kalembwa, ZAF Public Relations representative (statement)
a6265.speech: Issued the statement in which Commander Barry was speaking, after Barry surprised the ZAF No. 15 Air Defence Unit on an outdoor operation led by Air Officer Commanding, Brig Gen Mukuka Mwansa in Kasama, Northern Province.

a6332.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a6332.speech: According to WFP, West and Central Africa are on the brink of a humanitarian catastrophe: more than 36 million people are currently struggling to feed themselves in the region, a figure that could climb to more than 52 million during the lean season from June to August 2025, and WFP needs 700 million dollars to assist the most vulnerable people over the next three months.

a6332.speaker: Sib Ollo, senior regional adviser for research, assessment and monitoring at WFP
a6332.speech: “The food situation in the Sahel remains dramatic. We have visited communities facing unprecedented droughts in some areas, and floods in others, causing massive losses of crops and livestock.” ; “Selling a goat today is no longer even enough to buy half a sack of millet.” ; “Everywhere, we hear the same heartbreaking accounts. The time to act is now!” ; “Life-saving activities must take priority. A massive investment is needed to scale up operations.”

a6332.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a6332.speech: Beyond the emergency, WFP is calling for structural change; since 2018 its integrated resilience programme has made it possible to rehabilitate more than 300,000 hectares of land and to help four million people in 3,400 villages of the Sahel.

a6690.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a6690.speech: Assured today that it is closely following the situation of Cabo Verdean emigrants in the United States, in the face of the measures adopted by the new North American president; acknowledging the expectation surrounding migration policies, it stated that a team has been monitoring the evolution of the issue and its implications for the emigrant community.

a6788.speaker: Port authorities of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou
a6788.speech: Said that Vincent Bolloré came to the port solely to see the progress of the quay and terminal construction works that his group is building there; the authorities remain doubtful about the reported extradition deal and believe that Vincent Bolloré made a purely professional visit that in no way went beyond the framework of his group's investments.

a6788.speaker: Head of the communication service of the Port of Cotonou
a6788.speech: Said Vincent Bolloré's visit is one of the routine visits he makes to Benin to check on the progress of the works, and that the port is currently awaiting further investment from the second MCC compact while it is urgent that the other works be completed quickly: "At the port with Vincent Bolloré, there was no talk of the arrest or extradition of Patrice Talon, and we think that elsewhere (the Marina) it was not discussed either." Added that the current Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, Kassim Traoré, is very preoccupied with resolving the urgent matters on the port platform and shares, like the Head of State, the dream of making the port one of the most modern and largest in the sub-region, in order to meet the demands of a growing clientele.

a6788.speaker: Vincent Bolloré, CEO of the Bolloré group
a6788.speech: Emphasised the importance of the financial component and the advantages that the port of Cotonou will be able to draw in the coming years from this financing, which will propel the port into the ranks of the modern ports of the world.

a6788.speaker: La Nouvelle Tribune (the newspaper's own earlier article)
a6788.speech: Had asserted that "Bolloré is not a philanthropist and in return he must expect something. Behind the scenes, we learn that Boni Yayi is said to have promised the PVI, the railways and Bénin Télécoms to Vincent Bolloré. In return, the latter was to help the government in its obsessive desire to arrest Talon."

a6795.speaker: Bruce Wharton, US deputy assistant secretary of state, and Deborah Malac, US ambassador to Kampala
a6795.speech: Gave two reasons for their walk-out: the presence of Sudan's President Omar al-Bashir and President Museveni's reference to the International Criminal Court as “a bunch of useless people”.

a6795.speaker: African leaders present at the swearing-in (anonymous)
a6795.speech: Leaders told the author that the US diplomats' theatrics were an insult not just to President Museveni but to all of Africa.

a6795.speaker: Yoweri Museveni, President of Uganda
a6795.speech: Referred to the International Criminal Court as “a bunch of useless people” in his inaugural address.

a6795.speaker: US State Department
a6795.speech: Was peeved by the home arrest of the opposition's flagbearer.

a6795.speaker: Congress Blog (@congressblog), social-media post
a6795.speech: “The Hill Amateur theatrics: An insult to Africa: Last week, I watched with dismay as two American diplomats w… https://t.co/LEkcL9Fu9K” (May 19, 2016).

a6797.speaker: Sputnik correspondent
a6797.speech: Reports that hundreds of people took to the streets in the capital of Niger to take part in a protest against neocolonialism.

a6797.speaker: Protesters in Niamey
a6797.speech: Expressed support for the ruling National Council for the Defense of the Fatherland, thanking it for its steps to remove the country from the sphere of influence of the United States and France.

a6797.speaker: Group of military personnel from the presidential guard in Niger
a6797.speech: Announced in July 2023 the removal of the head of state Mohamed Bazoum.

a7195.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi and incoming COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Indicated that, in order to promote integration, Burundi is abolishing short-stay visas for COMESA member countries ; specified that Burundi is abolishing short-stay visas for nationals of COMESA member countries.

a7195.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi and incoming COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Welcomed his counterparts who honoured the proceedings with their presence, the Prime Ministers, the parliamentarians and other delegations, and stressed that Burundi is the crossroads, the intersection of different communities on the continent, while indicating that Burundi is a hub, a platform of a vast regional market.

a7195.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi and incoming COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Expressed his joy at having received his counterparts and other delegations to discuss the subjects that are dear to the COMESA region: "The Summit is an opportunity for us to assess ourselves and to plan together the future projects of our community. The latter has already reached maturity, and this is the great moment to plan in order to improve the living conditions of the populations."

a7195.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi and incoming COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Placed emphasis on the agricultural sector, indicating that it is the pillar of the region's economy and that agriculture is the largest job-providing activity in the region, although threatened by climate change; stressed that mining is likewise a lever of the region's economic development and included tourism among the growth-bearing sectors; shared Burundi's ambition to achieve food self-sufficiency so as also to have a surplus to sell abroad.

a7195.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of Burundi and incoming COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Expressed his firm commitment to work for the development of COMESA.

a7195.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Presented the achievements of the community during his presidency: from 2020 to 2023 extra-COMESA trade (exports outside COMESA) rose from 100 billion US dollars to two hundred and nineteen billion US dollars, while intra-COMESA trade went from ten billion US dollars in 2020 to fourteen billion US dollars in 2023.

a7195.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA Chairman
a7195.speech: Insisted on the necessity and importance of promoting trade among COMESA member countries and boosting investment: "Africa belongs to us, we must make great efforts to develop trade between our countries and to strengthen economic integration," while specifying that the results already achieved suggest that more must be done in this area ; called on member countries to do everything to prioritize economic integration and stability in the region, recalling the very negative impact of instability on daily life and on the economy in the region.

a7195.speaker: Other Heads of State and Government and delegations at the summit
a7195.speech: In their interventions, those who took the floor expressed their commitments to the achievement of COMESA's objectives, and mentioned certain achievements in various areas and the prospects of their respective countries which will contribute to those objectives.

a7378.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia (media statement)
a7378.speech: Commended Biden's decision to remove Cuba from the list of state sponsors of terrorism and welcomed the announcement, reaffirming Namibia's long-standing support for Cuba. ; "I commend the US government for having eventually taken the long-overdue decision to remove Cuba from the list of state sponsors of terrorism. Namibia has consistently advocated for the removal of Cuba from the list, deeming it arbitrary, unjust and with no basis in international law." ; Emphasised that while the decision marks progress, further action is still necessary to improve relations between the two nations: "This step should be followed by tangible actions by the US government to end the unjust and illegal economic blockade against Cuba."

a7378.speaker: Penda Naanda, executive director in the Namibian Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation
a7378.speech: "Namibia further believes that this move is expected to ease some economic restrictions and foster better understanding, as well as result in good diplomatic relations. Namibia is confident that this gesture by the outgoing US administration will contribute to strengthening international cooperation, and hopes that the incoming administration will continue to maintain the same diplomatic posture for the mutual benefit of the two countries and peoples." ; Added that the latest development could pave the way for further cooperation and mutual understanding between Cuba and the US, especially in the economic and social arenas.

a7378.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a7378.speech: During his two-day State visit to Cuba late last year, had labelled the ongoing blockade against Cuba as the most enduring and inhumane trade embargo in modern history.

a7465.speaker: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
a7465.speech: Said this week that while cases first recorded in October have spread to 23 of Nigeria's 36 states, nearly half of the deaths, 74, were reported this year.

a7465.speaker: local partners
a7465.speech: Described the recent rise in fatalities as “alarming”.

a7465.speaker: Sani Datti, NCDC spokesperson
a7465.speech: Told The Associated Press that most deaths from the disease have been mainly due to infected people not going to health facilities or arriving there late with severe complications, a common problem in past outbreaks in the country.

a7465.speaker: health providers (in northern Nigeria)
a7465.speech: Have warned the outbreak is rapidly spreading in hard-to-reach areas.

a7465.speaker: World Health Organisation
a7465.speech: Meningitis “is a major public health challenge for a country already grappling with ‘the world's highest burden of malaria’”, according to the World Health Organisation.

a7465.speaker: local officials
a7465.speech: Described the first batch of more than 1 million vaccine doses from the global vaccine alliance Gavi as a crucial milestone in disease response.

a7465.speaker: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
a7465.speech: Also said it is working with state authorities to scale up disease surveillance with a focus on tracking new cases, laboratory testing, and public sensitisation campaigns to curb the outbreak.

a7465.speaker: local partners
a7465.speech: Say access to hospitals remains a huge problem.

a7465.speaker: Simba Tirima, Nigeria country representative for French medical charity Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
a7465.speech: “We have seen hundreds of admissions and scores of deaths in just a few weeks. The high fatality rate is due to access (to) care, there are challenges with that and low vaccination coverage” ; told the AP that the most vulnerable are residents in remote areas who often arrive late to MSF facilities ; “We know that meningitis progresses rapidly, and patients' (conditions) can deteriorate in 24 hours,” calling for mass vaccination campaigns.
